source_spans.locator: Journal of Risk and Uncertainty 5, published p.297, abstract: cumulative rather than separable weighting; extension to uncertain prospects and any number of outcomes; distinct gain/loss weighting functions
Journal of Risk and Uncertainty 5, published pp.299-301, model development: outcomes ordered relative to a reference level and transformed into subjective values
Journal of Risk and Uncertainty 5, published pp.300-302, cumulative representation: decision weights derived from changes in transformed cumulative probabilities over ranked outcomes

Journal of Risk and Uncertainty 5, published p.303 and following model discussion: separate gain/loss value and weighting behavior with diminishing sensitivity and asymmetric treatment around the reference level

conditions: finite uncertain option with possible outcomes ordered relative to a reference level
task: evaluate and compare uncertain options with multiple possible outcomes

nodes.description: reference level that partitions possible outcomes into positive and negative changes
possible outcomes ordered by magnitude and partitioned by sign relative to the reference level
subjective values assigned to the ordered outcome changes by a nonlinear transform
probabilities or event weights associated with the possible outcomes
separate nonlinear transforms applied to cumulative probability mass on the positive and negative sides of the reference level
weights for individual ranked outcomes derived as differences between adjacent transformed cumulative masses
aggregate evaluation obtained by combining transformed outcome values with the derived rank-dependent weights

relations.description: the reference level partitions and orders outcomes into positive and negative regions before aggregation
probability mass is first accumulated according to outcome rank and sign, transformed, and differenced to produce per-outcome weights
each outcome change relative to the reference level is transformed into a subjective value
the aggregate option evaluation combines subjective outcome values with the derived rank-dependent weights
the cumulative construction adds ordering-sensitive structure beyond assigning a separable transformed weight to each outcome probability independently
